newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to firm, Nomura impact limited.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to firm, Nomura impact limited.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to firm on Wednesday, with little negative impact expected from the filing of a criminal complaint against Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Tuesday by Japan's securities watchdog with prosecutors, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the Nikkei average lost 14.40 points or 0.07 percent to 20,129.11. Its June futures fell 10 to 20,180.

"The market has had a lot of time to digest the Nomura scandal," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager, said. "If there is any effect on Nomura shares or the stock market, it will probably be short-lived."

Government sources said Tuesday that Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) filed a criminal complaint with prosecutors alleging that Nomura, two former executives and a former general manager compensated a client for investment losses.
The Finance Ministry also said it was suspending Nomura from Japanese government bond auctions and bond underwriting until the implementation of administrative punishments proposed by the SESC.
Nomura shares in London lost 35 yen from the Tokyo closing level to 1,515.
Brokers said that trade was likely to focus once again on sectors that have lagged behind the market such as textiles and shipbuilding,
Eyes will also be on Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), which briefly hit a new calendar year high of 1,020,000 yen on Tuesday as investors sought domestic-demand related issues.
"Blue chips are slowing down because of the strengthening yen against the dollar, and so shares such as NTT are in the limelight," one broker said.
"If trade in NTT's shares becomes more active, private investors will join in and power the market in general," he added.

Market sources said selling pressure was intense above 20,500 and gains would be difficult. But on the other hand, turnover was growing steadily and the downside was also likely to be limited near the 20,000 line.
Oil was the top losing sector. Air transport, banks and warehouses followed brokerages.

Gaining sectors were headed by telecommunications, lifted partly by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT) Corp, which matched its calendar year high at midday, after gaining 21,000 yen to 1.02 million. Investors continued to buy the domestic-demand reliant shares, brokers said.
They were also after low-priced issues in a bid to bring them up to a level matching the recent surge in the Nikkei average and the stock market in general, brokers said.
Sectors such as sea transport, retailers and shipbuilding gained as a result of such moves.
